Top News
 
 
 
 CPI and big bank earnings take center stage 
 
 
 
travelism/iStock via Getty Images
 
 
 Wall Street heads into a busy week with the September consumer price report and the kickoff of third-quarter earnings season likely to set the tone for markets.

 The CPI report arrives Wednesday at 8:30 a.m. ET, with economists expecting core inflation to rise 2.4%. Investors will be watching for any signs that price pressures are reaccelerating, particularly after the recent rally in yields and renewed concern over the inflation outlook.

 Earnings season also moves into higher gear. JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), Goldman Sachs ( GS ), Wells Fargo ( WFC ) and Citigroup ( C ) report Tuesday, followed by Bank of America ( BAC ), Morgan Stanley ( MS ) and BlackRock ( BLK ) on Wednesday.

 Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) reports Thursday in a key read for the AI chip complex, while Tesla ( TSLA ) is expected to unveil its next-generation Roadster the same day. Apple ( AAPL ) will also hold a smart-home product event Tuesday.

 Elsewhere, the Fed releases its Beige Book Wednesday, the September producer price report is due Thursday, and the Paris Auto Show runs throughout the week.

 Investing Group Spotlight 
 
 
 Energy markets remain on edge as geopolitical tensions threaten global oil supplies, creating potential opportunities for investors. In their latest article, Robert & Sam Kovacs examine how the evolving conflict, rising oil futures prices, and attractive valuations could shape the outlook for energy stocks. Their analysis highlights key opportunities, including Petrobras, and explores why select energy producers may be well positioned for further gains.

 ( Free Full Article ) Here’s a brief summary of the article:

 Robert & Sam reiterate a bullish outlook on the energy sector, arguing that the Iran conflict and escalating threats to key shipping routes could keep oil prices elevated for longer than markets anticipate. Seven stocks recommended in March delivered an equal-weighted return of 33%, outperforming the S&P 500’s 14.5% and the Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF’s 14.4%. While acknowledging imperfect timing, the author emphasizes the importance of building resilient positions that can withstand volatility.

 A key development is the rising 12-month oil futures price, which could support higher valuations for energy producers even as near-term crude prices fluctuate. The author remains positive on Canadian producers and Equinor, while beginning to take partial profits in tanker stocks after strong gains. Petrobras remains a standout opportunity, benefiting from elevated seaborne oil prices, a narrowing governance discount, and potential political changes in Brazil.

 Robert & Sam see scope for further valuation expansion, with a base-case price target of $33 per ADR and potential upside to $40 if oil supply disruptions persist. Overall, they maintain a strong conviction in Atlantic Basin producers, particularly Petrobras.
